situation: they worked in IT for a bank in the City of London before 2007
choice: they quit their job to play poker professionally
outcome: they struggled to find employment afterward and only secured a new job in early 2011 after extensive checks
main_reason: they wanted to pursue a living playing poker
advice: hide the poker experience on a résumé if possible
quote: Eventually early in 2011 I found a group who was willing to take a chance on me.
author: TheMathemagician

situation: they were employed at a software firm in India, trained in testing but working on a Java project, and received an offer for a Java developer role elsewhere
choice: they resigned from their current job after receiving the new offer
outcome: their designation was changed to software test analyst in the experience and relieving letters
main_reason: they wanted to join the new company as a Java developer
advice: ensure the new employer is aware of the designation discrepancy and provide supporting documents
quote: My designation was software analyst when I attended interview and it is Software test analyst now.
author: Vishal

situation: they resigned their seventh job at Accenture after the company refused remote work
choice: they quit the job
outcome: they saw a psychiatrist and felt everything fell into place
main_reason: the employer would not allow them to work from home
advice: seek employers that explicitly offer remote work and ask about policies during interviews
author: Joe Strazzere

situation: The author was placed on a performance improvement plan by their employer to force a resignation or termination with cause.
choice: They accepted a negotiated settlement and resigned instead of being fired.
outcome: They received a severance payment and secured a new job before their notice period ended.
main_reason: The employer wanted them out and offered a settlement to avoid paying full severance.
advice: Negotiate a settlement if the company is trying to force you out to save on severance costs.
quote: I resigned in exchange for a sum rather less than the severance. I had a new job before the notice was up.
author: DJClayworth

situation: Author was hired by a contractor who lied about their expertise to win a government contract.
choice: Author resigned from the project after the contractor refused to correct the false promise to the client.
outcome: The client appreciated the honesty, pushed back on the contractor, and the author protected their reputation.
main_reason: The contractor insisted on keeping an impossible and unethical promise despite the author's objections.
advice: Prioritize honesty and reputation over short-term gains, even if it means leaving a difficult situation.
author: closetnoc

situation: Their wife faced a complex legal case that threatened her business, requiring extensive support.
choice: They quit their software architect job to help manage the legal battle and assist with the business.
outcome: The legal case was resolved successfully after several years, and they are now ready to return to software work.
main_reason: To support their overwhelmed wife and handle the legal and business challenges.
advice: They can highlight improved written communication and ability to simplify complex issues under pressure on their CV.
quote: The legal battle had to be fought through a number of courts, taking several years before it concluded (successfully thankfully).
author: abc123

situation: they were working at a job with no other position lined up
choice: they decided to quit their first job
outcome: their former employer continued operating without them
main_reason: they wanted to leave the job
advice: be helpful when leaving, don’t feel guilty, and you have no obligation to inform them in advance
quote: FWIW, when I quit my first job, I thought I was critical to their success and that they would have a hard time without me. Somehow, they survived.
author: Kristopher Johnson

situation: Author was placed in a role by a recruiter and believed it was temporary.
choice: Quit the job after 97 days, just past the 90-day retention threshold.
outcome: The company paid a large referral fee to the recruiter, causing the author distress.
main_reason: Author felt horrible about the company paying a fee due to their timing.
advice: Be honest and open about intentions to avoid wasting recruiters' time.
quote: I felt HORRIBLE when I found out the company had paid a referral fee of several thousand dollars to the recruiter. 7 days past the 90 day cutoff.
author: Keith

situation: The author was underpaid and their employer refused a salary review.
choice: The author accepted a counteroffer to stay after initially handing in their notice.
outcome: The promised pay review never happened, and the workplace culture became toxic.
main_reason: The employer guilt-tripped the author into staying with false promises.
advice: Make counteroffers official and treat resignation as final to avoid repetition.
quote: Regrettably, I stayed. The pay review never happened. I just got further promises that went unfulfilled.
author: flexi

situation: They were placed on academic probation at a university due to poor grades.
choice: They decided to leave the university, attend community college, and take art, music, and math classes.
outcome: They later earned a bachelor's degree and now have a fulfilling, meaningful career.
main_reason: The probation made them realize they were in the wrong school and major.
advice: Feedback that highlights problems can be more valuable than passing grades.
quote: Being put on academic probation was one of the best things that ever happened to me.
author: Todd Wilcox

situation: The author struggled with the heavy mathematics component of a Computer Science degree at a top UK university.
choice: They dropped out of the CS program and switched to an Information Technology degree at another university.
outcome: They graduated and built a successful career as a software developer without needing advanced mathematics.
main_reason: The author found the mathematical lectures too difficult and believed the IT degree offered more practical skills.
advice: Consider switching to a more practical degree if the mathematical focus does not align with your career goals.
quote: For me this has worked well as I've had a good career as a software developer since graduating.
author: Jimmy

situation: they spent three years studying undergraduate physics and were interested in theoretical physics
choice: they switched to pure mathematics and enrolled in a PhD program
outcome: they are now beginning a PhD at the intersection of pure maths and theoretical computer science
main_reason: they felt theoretical physics was a dead end with limited experimental progress
advice: they suggest auditing different classes, speaking to advisors, and showing enthusiasm beyond the school curriculum when applying to college
quote: After 3 years of undergraduate physics, I switched to pure mathematics and am now beginning a PhD at the intersection of pure maths and theoretical computer science.
author: Meep

situation: They studied physics but struggled and felt their understanding was not solid, leading them to consider a change.
choice: They switched to pure mathematics during their university years.
outcome: They are glad they made the switch to pure math.
main_reason: They lacked confidence in physics calculations and were drawn to proof‑writing and abstract reasoning in math.
advice: Consider whether your skills and interests align with the field before committing.
quote: I switched to pure math over the course of a year and I am glad I did.
author: NWMT

situation: The author worked on a research project in a field outside their own major.
choice: They changed their major to the new field and continued research there.
outcome: The author enjoyed the project and found the change to be a benefit.
main_reason: They enjoyed the research project in the new field very much.
advice: Consider if changing fields is costly or undesirable if you enjoy the new field more.
quote: I ended up enjoying the project so much that I changed my major and continued doing research in the new field.
author: KTK
